source_scope_note.note: The supplied hardware design explicitly names only the commands/features listed below. Its related-documents table refers to a separate “SIM800 Series AT Command Manual” (document [1]), which was not supplied; a family-level manual/catalog is not proof of per-model command support.

module_specific_features.feature: Set the four frequency bands; SIM800C can also search them automatically.
Power off SIM800C; the module logs off the network and sends the URC “NORMAL POWER OFF” before completion.
Read temperature when the module is running; temperature detection is stated to be disabled by default.
Sleep Mode 2; module enters automatically after no RXD data for over 5 seconds and no air/hardware interrupts.
Set functionality level 0 (minimum), 1 (full/default), or 4 (flight mode; RF disabled).
Set a fixed serial baud rate; the setting is saved automatically to non-volatile flash memory.
Read the auxiliary ADC voltage value.
Switch RF_SYNC between RF synchronization and RF-jamming-detection function.

reference_circuits.what_pdf_shows: Low-ESR 100 µF bypass recommendation; 100uF tantalum CA, 1uF~10uF ceramic CB, 33pF and 10pF capacitors, and a 5.1V/500mW Zener diode placed close to VBAT pins.
+5V input reference using MIC29302; text states 4.1V output. Figure labels input capacitors 100uF/1uF, C103 330uF, C104 100nF, R101 100K, R102 43K, and R103 470Ω.
Figure uses LM2596-ADJ with components labelled L101 100uH, FB101 270Ω, D102 MBR360, C101 100uF, C102 1uF, C103 330uF, C104 100nF, R101 2.2K, and R102 1K.
Figures 10 and 11 show transistor- and button-based power-on/down connections to the internally pulled-up PWRKEY.
Figures show VRTC RTC-core backup using a large-capacitance capacitor, a non-chargeable battery, or a rechargeable battery; each diagram labels a 1.5K element.
A 3.3V resistor-matching circuit (1K series; 5.6K resistors, changed to 14K for 3.0V), a diode-isolation circuit for 3.0/3.3V, and TX/RX level-matching circuits for 5V are shown.
USB_VBUS-to-VBUS, USB_DN and USB_DP with 22R series labels, GND, and a 1uF capacitor are shown.
UART1_TXD, UART1_RXD, GND, and PWRKEY connect to an I/O connector for UART upgrading/debugging.
SPKP/SPKN circuit shows 10pF and 33pF capacitors and ESD protection near the speaker.
MICP/MICN circuit to an electret microphone shows 10pF and 33pF capacitors, ESD protection, close microphone placement, and differential-layout notation.
Molex-91228 circuit with a 4.7K VDD_EXT connection, 51Ω resistors on SIM_RST/SIM_CLK/SIM_DATA, 22pF and 100nF capacitors, and ESDA6V1 is shown.
Amphenol C707 10M006 512 circuit with 51Ω SIM_RST/SIM_CLK/SIM_DATA resistors, 22pF and 100nF capacitors, and ESDA6V1 is shown.
VBAT, NETLIGHT, a 4.7K label, and a 47K label are shown.

Both with-RF-connector and without-RF-connector arrangements show GSM_ANT, R101, C101, and C102; text says matching values are antenna-design dependent and normally R101 is 0Ω while C101/C102 are not mounted.
BT_ANT circuit shows R201, C201, and C202; text says values are antenna-design dependent and normally R201 is 0R while C201/C202 are not mounted.

pcb_considerations.consideration: Power: keep VBAT return GND important; make the VBAT positive line short and wide; route source to VBAT through Zener diode then large capacitor; make pins 36/37 short to power-source GND; do not route signals above the 10 GND pads if possible.
Power: ensure input never drops below 3.0V during a 2A transmit burst; use at least 60mil PCB traces from VBAT to the supply and place power IC/bypass capacitor close to the module.
RF: make output-pin-to-connector trace as short as possible; do not route RF across the board; keep it away from the SIM card and power ICs.
SIM: place holder far from antenna/RF cable and near module; protect SIM_CLK, SIM_DATA, SIM_RST, and SIM_VDD with ESD components and keep them away from power/high-speed-frequency signals.

SIM: use short traces away from RF/VBAT/high-speed lines; connect holder GND directly to main ground; place 100nF on SIM_VDD near holder; TVS parasitic capacitance should not exceed 50pF; 51Ω on SIM_RST/SIM_CLK/SIM_DATA can enhance ESD protection.

Audio: keep audio traces away from antenna and power and avoid running them parallel to VBAT. Differential layout, RF-coupling filters, GND, and capacitor placement recommendations are provided for TDD-noise reduction.
Trace UART signal lines together; likewise trace USB signals together.

antenna_requirements.requirement: There are two antenna interfaces: GSM_ANT and BT_ANT.
Antenna input impedance should be 50Ω and VSWR should be less than 2.
Place GSM and BT antennas as far apart as possible; isolation should be bigger than 30dB.
Use a 50Ω microstrip or stripline antenna connection for GSM_ANT; reserve an antenna-design-dependent matching circuit.
Keep RF connector close to GSM_ANT for conducted test; keep matching circuit close to antenna; keep RF traces 50Ω and away from high-frequency/strong-interference sources.

protection_circuits.protection: VBAT surge protection: a 5.1V/500mW Zener diode is strongly recommended and should be placed close to VBAT; Table 6 lists suggested 500mW diode parts.
SIM interface: all SIM-interface signals should be protected against ESD with a TVS diode array.
SIM interface: recommended ESD parts include ST ESDA6V1-5W6 or ON SEMI SMF05C; place SIM peripheral components close to holder.
USB: TVS on USB data lines should be less than 5pF; USB data lines should be routed differentially.
Audio: speaker and microphone reference circuits depict ESD protection and 10pF/33pF capacitors.

communication.method_procedure: The document states that conducted output power is shown and follows 3GPP TS 05.05 technical-specification requirements; Tables 36 and 37 list PCL nominal output power and normal/extreme tolerances for GSM850/EGSM900 and DCS1800/PCS1900.
The document says conducted receiving sensitivity was tested under static condition. The table reports typical < -109dBm and max < -107dBm for GSM850/EGSM900 and DCS1800/PCS1900.

power.method_procedure: Figure 8 test conditions state VBAT=4.0V, CA=100µF tantalum with ESR=0.7Ω, and CB=1uF~10uF; the figure labels a 2A burst and “Max:350mV”.

environmental.method_procedure: Table 35 gives test conditions of temperature 25℃ and humidity 45%, then reports contact/air-discharge levels for VBAT, GND, UART1_TXD/UART1_RXD, antenna port, SPKP/SPKN/MICP/MICN, and PWRKEY.

missing_data.reason: No GNSS/GPS support statement appears in the supplied SIM800C Hardware Design V1.02 extract.
The supplied source refers to, but does not include, the SIM800 Series AT Command Manual; named commands are captured only where explicit in this document.
No named functional validation test procedure with results is documented in the supplied source; operational procedures/timings are not reported as validation tests.
The reported power, RF, and ESD tests give methods, conditions, values, or tolerances but do not state explicit pass/fail acceptance language.
A “Typical solder reflow profile of lead-free processes” figure is present, but its numeric axes/parameters are not recoverable from the supplied text extraction.
Only one actual SIM800C source edition (V1.02) was supplied. Its internal version-history page is not a second supplied edition for comparison.

ambiguities.detail: Physical PDF page numbers are derived from form-feed order. The initial segment before the first form feed contains only the document-control filename, while the following segment is printed page 2; citations use the required 1-based physical sequence.

Table 5 spans physical pages 13–15. On page 14, the text extraction groups MICP/MICN under one I/O cell and SPKP/SPKN under another, and groups GND pin numbers. Individual records retain the displayed grouped direction/function; blank GND direction/type is recorded as null.

Table 5 and the pin-assignment figure identify GSM_ANT as pin 32 and pin 33 as GND, but GSM antenna matching figures label GSM_ANT “(Pin33)” and also label a GND “(Pin33)”. Pinout uses the table/assignment value 32; matching-figure pin labels are internally inconsistent.
The pin-description table names pin 26 USB_DN, while the pin-assignment figure names pin 26 USB_DM. The pinout retains USB_DN from Table 5 and notes the source-label variation.

Physical pages 15 and 16 identify dimension/footprint figures and unit mm, but the supplied text extraction does not contain their dimension callouts. The separately printed 17.6*15.7*2.3mm textual specification is reported instead.

Table 34 header begins on page 42 and most rows appear on page 43. OCR/layout splits the table and misspells “Average currnet”; current entries are transcribed with their displayed mode/band labels and retained citations, but cell alignment is less certain than a native table.
The V1.02 source internally says version 1.02 updated Tables 1/2 and several figures, but no V1.00 or V1.01 source was supplied for a factual edition-to-edition comparison.
